comment: cowdiff states for f_100dc080 (cow_net_clock_seconds). The entry reads two words - the clock pointer at 0x10492e10 and the seconds field at object+0x0c - and a fuzzed state almost never has a readable pointer there, so without these it faults at the second read, both sides fault, and the one instruction that is the whole unit is never compared (measured: 3 of 4 blocks). Each state publishes the object in the arena and names the field; the sentinel at +0x10 is there because a conversion that wrote anything back would be caught by it. Bytes are RAW little-endian.

states.note: seconds = 7: the field comes back whole
seconds = 0xdeadbeef: the whole dword, not just a byte or a sign-extended half
the object published at a DIFFERENT address: a conversion that used the static block at COW_ADDR_FRAME_NET_CLOCK_OBJ instead of whatever the global holds is caught here
